args.text:
December 19th.

_Dear Daddy-Long-Legs_,

You never answered my question, and I'll have you know it was a dead important one.

ARE YOU BALD?

I've got you all worked out, top to toe--very satisfactorily, thanks very much--right up till I get to the top of your noggin, and then I _am_ stuck. Stuck fast. I can't make up my mind whether you've got white hair or black hair or a sort of sprinkly grey, salt-and-pepper job, or maybe nothing up there at all.

Here is your portrait:

But here's the hitch: do I give you some hair or don't I?

Want to know what colour your eyes are? They're grey, and your eyebrows stick out like a verandah roof over the front steps (beetling, they call them in novels, if you please), and your mouth's a straight line that's got a habit of turning down at the corners. Oh, you see, I know! You're a snappy old thing with a bit of a temper on you, I reckon.

(Chapel bell.)

9.45 P. M.

Right, I've got a new rule, and it's unbreakable: never, ever study at night, no matter how many written reviews are bearing down on me in the morning. Instead I read just plain books--I have to, you know, cos there are eighteen blank years behind me, the whole lot of them empty as a church on a Monday. You wouldn't believe it, Daddy, what an abyss of ignorance my mind is; I'm only just finding out how far down it goes myself. The things most girls with a properly assorted family and a home and friends and a library soak up without even trying, I've never so much as heard of. For example:

I never read "Mother Goose" or "David Copperfield" or "Ivanhoe" or "Cinderella" or "Blue Beard" or "Robinson Crusoe" or "Jane Eyre" or "Alice in Wonderland" or one single word of Rudyard Kipling. Not one. I didn't know Henry the Eighth was married more than once (more than once! the old goat), or that Shelley was a poet. I didn't know that people used to be monkeys and that the Garden of Eden was a beautiful myth. I didn't know R.L.S. stood for Robert Louis Stevenson, or that George Eliot was a lady. I'd never laid eyes on a picture of the "Mona Lisa", and (it's true, but you won't believe it) I'd never even heard of Sherlock Holmes. Fair dinkum.

Now I know all of those things and heaps more besides, but you can see how much catching up I've got to do. And oh, it's fun! I look forward to the evening all day long, and then I stick an "engaged" on the door, get into my beaut red bath robe and furry slippers, pile every cushion I own up behind me on the couch, light the brass student lamp at my elbow, and read and read and read till the cows come home. One book's not enough for me. I've got four on the go at once. Right now it's Tennyson's poems and "Vanity Fair" and Kipling's "Plain Tales" and--don't laugh--"Little Women." Turns out I'm the only girl in the whole college who wasn't brought up on "Little Women." I haven't let on to anybody, mind (that _would_ stamp me as queer). I just snuck off quietly and bought it with $1.12 of last month's allowance, and the next time somebody brings up pickled limes, I'll know exactly what she's on about!

(Ten o'clock bell. This is a very interrupted letter.)

Saturday.

_Sir_,

I have the honour to report fresh explorations in the field of geometry. On Friday last we downed tools on our former works in parallelopipeds and pushed on to truncated prisms. We are finding the road rough, sir, and very much uphill.

Sunday.

The Christmas holidays kick off next week and the trunks are up. The corridors are that chockers with them you can hardly squeeze through, and everybody's so bubbling over with excitement that the study's gone clean out the window. I'm going to have a ripper of a time over the holidays; there's another Freshman, who lives in Texas, staying behind as well, and we're planning to go on long walks and--if there's any ice about--learn to skate. Then there's still the whole library to get through--and three empty weeks to do it in!

Hooroo, Daddy, I hope you're feeling as happy as I am.

Yours ever,

JUDY.

P. S. Don't forget to answer my question. If you can't be bothered writing, get your secretary to send a telegram. He only has to say:

Mr. Smith is quite bald, or Mr. Smith is not bald, or Mr. Smith has white hair.

And you can take the twenty-five cents out of my allowance.

See ya in January--and a merry Chrissie!
